(2) msg-id minting versus daemon dedupe: the CLI now mints the value the daemon uses as the delivery dedupe key; re-sending with an explicit --msg-id still collapses to one row (the shipped-CLI duplicate assertion, run green). Worth knowing that two id SHAPES now share one field — the daemon mints `&lt;hex16&gt;-&lt;hex16&gt;`, the CLI mints a UUIDv7 — which is harmless because the field is opaque, but it is now true. (3) peek flag: CLI --peek to `?peek=true` to DeliveryService::peek_inbox to Queue::peek, traced end to end and exercised live; F3 is its test gap.<br><br>i6 JUDGEMENT — Queue::peek and pointer-worker concurrency. peek is correct and consistently specified. It selects the oldest row in state ('pending','running') for exactly this seat's delivery kind, ORDER BY id — the same ordering key claim uses — and writes nothing; the schema guard is applied first. It deliberately diverges from claim in three ways, and FakeQueue diverges identically in all three, so the contract test is not vacuous: neither honours `not_before`, neither excludes serial keys already running, and peek does not run claim's lease sweep. The consequences are worth naming rather than hiding: a peek can show a row another reader has already claimed and is seconds from acking, and can show a row parked for a retry that has not come due. Both err toward showing mail that might be gone rather than hiding mail that is still there, which is the same posture claim/ack already takes about duplicate reads. Pointer-worker concurrency is untouched by this plan — the worker still claims, peek is called from nowhere but the inbox route, and the worker's test fake merely delegates.<br><br>FLOWSPACE DOGFOOD (i1). `flowspace3 search 'resolve acting seat identity from pane or environment'` returned crates/daemon/src/http/identity.rs::resolve_seat as the top hit with an accurate smart summary, and surfaced crates/cli/src/main.rs alongside it — both ladders in one result set, which is precisely the comparison F1 rests on. The new untracked module is indexed (a `resolve_acting_seat` query returns crates/cli/src/identity.rs). One friction: the `flowspace` skill documents `flowspace3 search "&lt;concept&gt;" --mode semantic`, and this build rejects `--mode` outright (`error: unexpected argument '--mode' found`). Skill text and CLI have drifted. |

| F1 | defect | MAJOR | CRITICAL on the packet's scale. `resolve_acting_seat` builds an `IdentityRequest` carrying EITHER `seat` (when PIJ_SESSION_ID is non-empty) OR `pane` — never both, and never `caller`. The daemon's anti-impersonation guard in `resolve_seat` (crates/daemon/src/http/identity.rs:700-720) fires only when BOTH are present, so this call site never supplies the guard's inputs and the guard cannot fire. The result is a SECOND identity ladder in the CLI whose rule is the opposite of the daemon's: a PIJ_SESSION_ID naming another seat silently wins over the pane the caller is actually sitting in. This is looser than what shipped BEFORE the plan for `report`: plan 117 deliberately moved report onto the daemon ladder so a write verb could not name a subject it had not derived, and resolve_seat's docstring says in as many words that two ladders are 'two places for the anti-impersonation posture to drift apart, which this repo has already paid for elsewhere'. Note that main.rs already holds the correct constructor one screen away — `identity_request()` (crates/cli/src/main.rs:883) passes seat AND pane AND caller context, with the comment 'the daemon still refuses if the answer would be an impersonation' — and the new module does not use it. It also contradicts the plan's own G1 ('a supplied --from/--seat that DISAGREES with the pane owner is refused by name, never silently honoured'), because the disagreement the CLI checks is against the ENV value, not against the pane owner. | crates/cli/src/identity.rs:36-52 | — | PROOF (isolated daemon 127.0.0.1:17931, own state dir, throwaway seats and tmux session, all torn down; production untouched).<br><br>Seats: pij-carol owns pane %3105, pij-dave owns pane %3106 — both registered with live pids and real proc_start values.<br><br>Sitting in CAROL's pane while asserting DAVE's id:<br>  $ PIJ_SESSION_ID=pij-dave TMUX_PANE=%3105 pij-rs send --to pij-carol --body who-am-i<br>  {"ok":true,...,"meta":"from pij-dave; msg_id 01a0603e-5867-7a90-ad61-f858feae7612"}<br>and the mail actually lands attributed to the impersonated seat:<br>  $ PIJ_SESSION_ID=pij-carol pij-rs inbox --peek<br>  {"ok":true,...,"data":[{"from":"pij-dave","to":"pij-carol","body":"who-am-i",...}]}<br><br>The SAME environment, one verb over:<br>  $ PIJ_SESSION_ID=pij-dave TMUX_PANE=%3105 pij-rs whoami<br>  {"ok":false,...,"meta":"the caller claims to be `pij-dave` but pane `%3105` belongs to `pij-carol` — refusing rather than answering for either. An asserted id never outranks an observable one.","error":"refused"}<br>One daemon, one environment, two opposite answers. `whoami` refuses because it goes through `identity_request`; `send` does not because it goes through the new module.<br><br>The same bypass on a WRITE that mutates another seat's card (earlier seats pij-alice %77 / pij-bob %88):<br>  $ PIJ_SESSION_ID=pij-bob TMUX_PANE=%77 pij-rs report now "impersonated did" "impersonated next"<br>  {"ok":true,...,"data":{"line":"reported by pij-bob: ...","seat":"pij-bob","seq":3}}<br>and `pij-rs state pij-bob` then carries statusPrev "impersonated did" while pij-alice's card is untouched. Written from alice's pane, recorded against bob.<br><br>The author's own suite encodes the bypass rather than catching it: crates/cli/tests/spawn.rs sends with envs [("PIJ_SESSION_ID","pij-sender"),("TMUX_PANE","%wrong")] and asserts SUCCESS. A pane that contradicts the asserted id is presented as a passing case.<br><br>SMALLEST FIX: in `resolve_acting_seat`, always send both — `IdentityRequest { seat: env, pane, caller: Some(caller_context()), ..default() }`, i.e. reuse main.rs's `identity_request` — and let the daemon rule. One decision comes with it, and it is the PM's or prime's to make, not mine: with both fields present, a caller whose pane is unknown to the rs store (legacy-registered seats, paneless harnesses) now hits `no live seat in the rs store owns pane '%N'` even though its env id is valid. Retrying seat-only on THAT SPECIFIC refusal preserves today's reach while keeping the impersonation case refused, because impersonation is the case where the pane IS owned — by someone else. What must not survive the fix is a CLI that decides identity precedence on its own. | — | — | — | — |
| F2 | defect | MINOR | MEDIUM. `inbox` now resolves an acting seat BEFORE it considers `--seat`, so a shell with neither PIJ_SESSION_ID nor a registered TMUX_PANE can no longer read ANY inbox — including the non-destructive `--peek`, which needs no acting identity to be safe. `pij inbox --seat &lt;id&gt;` was documented as 'the explicit operator/debug path' (docs/plans/108-rust-port/assets/reports/done-u-inbox.md:14) and used as such in the field (docs/plans/118-message-framing/execution.log.md:19, where a recipient recovered a parked message with `pij-rs inbox --seat pij-dominant-vicuna`). Refusing the DESTRUCTIVE cross-seat form is AC6 working as ruled and is not the complaint; losing the operator's observation path with it is a side effect nothing in the plan asked for. | crates/cli/src/main.rs:604-628 | — | PROOF: env -u PIJ_SESSION_ID -u TMUX_PANE pij-rs inbox --seat pij-alice --peek → {"ok":false,...,"meta":"pij inbox: no acting seat: set PIJ_SESSION_ID or run from a registered tmux pane (TMUX_PANE); --from/--seat may assert agreement but cannot create identity"}. Identical refusal with and without --peek, so the flag that AC6 designates as the safe cross-seat read is unreachable from an unregistered shell.<br><br>SMALLEST FIX (PM's call between two): either resolve the acting seat only when it is NEEDED — for `--peek` with an explicit `--seat`, skip the ladder, since peek claims and acks nothing — or keep the refusal and make it name the remaining path ('re-run with PIJ_SESSION_ID=&lt;your id&gt;'), and record in the plan that the paneless operator read is gone on purpose. Either is defensible; silently losing it is not. | — | — | — | — |
